public_rationale: Reporting supports the Arrakis setback: the project was canceled after inadequate performance, disappointing hopes for a cheaper model. It does not establish the precise late-2023 delivery timing. The broader efficiency claim is contradicted under the ordinary operating-efficiency reading: in June 2023 OpenAI explicitly reported efficiency savings that it was passing to developers. That is stronger evidence than a price cut alone, although it remains a company disclosure without independent cost measurements.
limitations: The Arrakis evidence is a secondary account of inaccessible original reporting.
The efficiency finding concerns operating systems, including serving models; it does not establish improved training efficiency or isolate model architecture.
A narrower reading limited to architecture-level efficiency would remain unresolved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has failed to make its models more efficient, including failing to deliver the Arrakis model to Microsoft in late 2023.

our_interpretation: Assess the historical record through publication; the statement names no beginning, so leave the period's start unspecified.
Read efficiency as reduced resources or operating cost for comparable model work, including serving improvements.
Treat the broad efficiency claim and the specific Arrakis setback as distinct components of the same claim.
Lower customer prices alone do not prove lower operating costs.
Based on reporting describes the evidentiary basis, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting establishes the Arrakis delivery failure, and evidence supports the broader claim that OpenAI had failed to achieve efficiency improvements through July 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence documents achieved operating efficiencies before publication, or establishes that Arrakis was successfully delivered as described. Support for the setback alongside contrary evidence on the broader record warrants mixed.
